requirement_text: The international admission pathway is designed for all candidates who are preparing to sit for a non-French secondary school certificate or diploma. Indeed, what matters in the choice of the pathway is the type of secondary school diploma, not the candidate's nationality. [...] If you are preparing for both the French baccalaureate and a non-French secondary school diploma, you must apply through the French admission pathway, on Parcoursup. [...] If you are preparing for an Abibac, a Bachibac or an Esabac in a French high school, you must apply through the French admission pathway on Parcoursup. If you are preparing for a European Baccalaureate, an Abibac, a Bachibac or an Esabac in a non-French high school, you must apply to the Bachelor through the international admission pathway, except for the dual degree programmes between Sciences Po and a French university to which you must apply via Parcoursup.
researcher_notes: Which admissions pathway/platform applies is itself the fact to record, per the research brief. Sciences Po runs two entirely separate platforms: Parcoursup (French/European-Bac track) and its own admissions website (International Admission Pathway, for any other non-French secondary diploma -- IB, A-levels, Abitur, Maturite suisse, US HSD, etc.). Eligibility is determined by diploma track, not nationality, and by Sciences Po's own words 'it is the responsibility of the applicant to find out which pathway applies to their circumstances.'

requirement_text: candidates are eligible to enter Sciences Po in the first year of the Undergraduate College if they are currently enrolled in study for a French Baccalaureate, or an equivalent foreign diploma of secondary education. They must be preparing to sit these assessments for the first time, over the course of the academic year underway. [...] Applicants who have obtained their Baccalaureate or equivalent foreign diploma in the 12 months prior to sending off their application may be permitted to apply, as an exception and on certain conditions. In particular, the candidate should not have been enrolled at another institution of higher education during all or part of these twelve months.
researcher_notes: Standard case is applying while still enrolled and sitting the diploma for the first time in the current academic year; the 12-month-post-graduation exception is conditional, not automatic (requires not having enrolled in other higher education in that window, including Sciences Po prep classes).

requirement_text: candidates are awarded two marks out of 20 and one out of 10, for a total of 50 points. [Evaluation 1: secondary school exams. Evaluation 2: candidate's academic performance and progress. Evaluation 3: academic project and motivations.] In order to proceed to the next step, candidates must obtain a mark equal to or higher than a minimum mark defined by Sciences Po each year. This minimum mark will be established by the admissions jury officially, after examination of the results and in view of the quality of applications. [...] After the interview, which is also graded out of 50, the jury totals the four marks to give a final mark out of 100. Candidates must obtain or exceed a minimum admissions mark defined annually by the university.
researcher_notes: DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED AS A NUMERIC THRESHOLD, per the scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md finding and the coordinator's brief: Sciences Po's own page states the pass mark at both the written-application stage (/50) and the final stage (/100) is set 'annually' by the admissions jury 'after examination of the results and in view of the quality of applications' for that specific year -- i.e. it depends on the rest of that cycle's applicant field, the same structural shape as a French concours even though Sciences Po's own process is not formally called one. No score is published in advance that a student can be told they need. Recording a specific number here would be a fabrication; recording the structure (4 weighted evaluations, 2 gated stages, jury-set variable bar) is the honest representation.

requirement_text: Attaching proof of language proficiency (such as language tests) at the time of application is entirely optional. You must, however, ensure that your language skills match the requirements of the programmes you are applying to [...] During the interview (as well as via the texts submitted), candidates will be tested on their language proficiency (in English and/or French, based on the programmes they are applying to). Should the level be insufficient, the interview panel reserves the right to issue a negative opinion.
researcher_notes: Another explicitly non-scalar requirement: Sciences Po does NOT require a submitted TOEFL/IELTS/DELF/DALF score at all for undergraduate admission -- proficiency is assessed qualitatively through the written texts and the interview itself, per programme language of instruction (French and/or English, varies by campus/track). A specific test-score threshold was not found because none is published; this is a genuine absence, not a gap in this research pass. Per-campus/per-track specific language-of-instruction requirements (Dijon/Le Havre/Menton/Nancy/Paris/Poitiers/Reims) exist on the same page behind collapsed accordion sections not captured by plain-text extraction -- flagged as not individually researched this pass, not as confirmed absent.

requirement_text: As the 150 euros application fees are non refundable.
researcher_notes: Application fee, EUR150, explicitly stated as non-refundable.

requirement_text: Candidates who have obtained the necessary mark will be invited to an interview, which is the fourth and final evaluation for admission. [...] The interview takes place remotely, and consists of three stages: The candidate introduces themselves; The candidate is asked to choose between 2 images which they will comment on and analyse; The candidate and the examiners will discuss their motivations.
researcher_notes: Mandatory second stage, gated on clearing the first written-application evaluation.
